items.title: Crescent City Crystals: Dave Bailey, Harold Christophe, Albert Delone, Sylvester Handy Interview, 1963-11-13
items.q: You played with the Sam Morgan band? Mm-hmm.

ctx.x: Born in New Orleans and the Trimmy.

Trimmy? Oh, I know. From Trimmy to the Rocky Green. Like London Avenue. 7-Watt, you know? What... Who taught you to play guitar? Now, who taught me how to play guitar? My father played guitar, you see? Yeah. But my first instrument, I used to pick up his guitar. Uh-huh. And all that harmony was right in my head. Yeah. Sure, I guess from listening to him, you pick up... Yeah, and definitely I would get beaten for fooling the guitar. Yeah. You know what I mean? Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. But then I started out on the…

items.title: Harold Christophe Interview, 1961-08-01
items.q: I'd say Sam Morgan... Sam had held the city for many years. Went all on the coast and everywhere with Sam Morgan.

ctx.x: Who were your favorite trumpet players? Who did you like to play with? Who were the best ones in the city and all that you heard those days?

Well, I'll tell you, we had quite a few good trumpet players. I'd say Sam Morgan, Buddy P. King, and we had Punch. He was a nice trumpet player at that time. Rain A was one of the next greatest to Sam Morgan, I think, with Tornation. But Sam had a sweet Tornation at the time. And Rain A, he come with the best second tone of the city that we know. We had several good ones. And probably all of them was good back in them days. But they had different favorites and so forth like that. Well, Buddy T. P., we would say…
Yeah, the tune and something like that.
